dish: Old-school $2.50 bak chor mee & fishball noodles
address: 80 Circuit Road, #02-10, Block 80 Market & Food Centre, Singapore 370080
w: One of the last hawker stalls in Singapore still selling noodles from S$2.50 — old-school bak chor mee and fishball noodles tossed in chilli-and-mushroom sauce with handmade wontons. The senior couple, at Circuit Road since 2006 (the name comes from stall no.10 at NUS Engineering's canteen), keep the price down for the neighbourhood's elderly; Mothership profiled their refusal to raise it.

dish: Sliced fish / fish head soup in 8-hour bone-and-chicken broth
n: Yong Lai Fa Ji Shu Shi
address: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-66, 79/79A Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
w: A Circuit Road fish-soup stall rated by veteran bloggers as on par with the famous Amoy Street bowl — fresh, bouncy fish in a robust broth simmered from fish bones and chicken for at least eight hours, with the fried sole-fish (ti poh) and ikan bilis made in-house. Fish soup around S$4.

dish: Halal Thai beef noodles in clove-scented refillable broth
address: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-54, 79 Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
w: A hidden-gem halal Thai beef-noodle stall at Circuit Road — the signature bowl (S$6) piles three forms of beef over kangkong and bean sprouts in a light, clear yet beefy broth (free refills) simmered at least three hours, fragrant with cloves and fried garlic. Reviewed by all three of the major SG food titles.

dish: Old-school lor mee with crispy yam & thick starchy gravy
address: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-07, 79/79A Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
w: A single-dish lor mee stall that has sustained itself since the 1970s on one bowl done well — a strong, savoury, gently vinegary gravy with crispy fried yam and plain hard-boiled egg, the thick starchy sauce slurpable to the last. From S$3, with a bigger S$5 portion; the boss is famously courteous.

dish: Top-10-ranked mee siam, plus laksa & lor mee
n: Hup Hup Mee Siam・Laksa・Lor Mee
address: Block 80 Circuit Road Market & Food Centre (Level 2), 80 Circuit Road, Singapore 370080
w: Second-generation hawker Joseph's Circuit Road stall, named a Top 10 Mee Siam in Singapore by Shin Min Daily News — a peanut-rich, addictively sour-and-light gravy (S$3). The laksa and an 'converted me into a lor mee lover' lor mee (S$4-5, packed with tau pok, hum and fish cake) round out the trio.

dish: Char siew rice & roasted pork noodles
address: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, 79/79A Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
w: A Cantonese roast-meats stall at Circuit Road turning out char siew rice (from S$4) and roasted-pork noodles (S$4.50) alongside its roast duck — a value roast-meats standby both SPH lifestyle titles single out in their Circuit Road round-ups.

dish: Hefty artisanal sandwiches, sourdough & specialty coffee
address: The Poiz Centre, 51 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 347697
w: Young owner Shan Chew's under-the-radar Potong Pasir sandwich cafe, drawing foodies island-wide for a tight menu of hefty sandwiches (the Breakfast Sandwich with candied bacon; a juicy Wagyu patty melt), sourdough and sustainable specialty coffee — with pizzas after 6pm. A Time Out and Eatbook favourite of the estate.

dish: $5 kam heong crab claws & Penang-style char kway teow
address: 83 MacPherson Lane, Singapore 360083
w: A value-for-money zi char stall in a MacPherson Lane coffeeshop that went viral for restaurant-grade shellfish at hawker prices — crab claws at S$5 each (four kam-heong claws for S$20), salted-egg crab around S$30 — and, unexpectedly, one of the better Penang-style char kway teow around, which is what drew ieatishootipost.

dish: Signature honeydew prawns served in the melon
n: Yi Jia South Village Seafood Restaurant
address: 544 MacPherson Road, Singapore 368225
w: A zi char that grew from a Toa Payoh coffeeshop into a full seafood restaurant on MacPherson Road, famed for its signature honeydew prawns — wild-caught ang kah prawns in a secret honeydew-melon sauce, served inside the melon itself — plus salted-egg crab and curry fish head. A long-running favourite of the veteran hawker bloggers.

dish: Japanese donburi under $10 (caramelised char siew don)
address: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
w: Young hawkerpreneur Xiao Xuan and her mother's donburi stall (started 2022 at Bukit Canberra) brings Japanese rice bowls under S$10 to Woodleigh Village — a Caramelised Char Siew Don (S$7) of smoky-sweet pork belly with a sous-vide egg, plus mentaiko chicken katsu and Angus sukiyaki dons.

dish: Wanton mee with ngoh hiang & chicken cutlet
address: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
w: A wholesome, budget-friendly wanton mee at Woodleigh Village — springy egg noodles with char siew, wontons and sides of ngoh hiang and chicken cutlet — repeatedly named among the centre's best-value stalls across the SethLui, Daniel Food Diary and Eatbook guides.

dish: Halal wok-hei fried rice (egg, sambal, hae bee hiam)
address: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-11, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
w: Young hawker Nam's halal-certified fried-rice specialist at Woodleigh Village, plating several styles — Egg Fried Rice (S$3.20), sambal, curry and hae bee hiam — from a stall HungryGoWhere featured in its 'Hawker Hustlers' series. One of the young-entrepreneur stalls that defined the new centre.

dish: Steamed & roasted chicken rice value sets
address: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-28, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
w: The Woodleigh outlet of the well-followed Whampoa Nan Xiang chicken rice, helmed by the owner's son Shaun — silky, tender steamed or roasted chicken with fragrant rice, portions from S$4.50, popular for its value sets.

dish: White curry prawn noodles
address: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-31, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
w: A young-hawker stall billed as serving Singapore's first white curry prawn noodles — a milder, creamy take on curry laksa built on a prawn base — one of the cross-cuisine newcomers Eatbook picked out among Woodleigh Village's young hawkers.

dish: Kaya toast, nasi lemak & mee rebus in an industrial cafe
address: 45 Tai Thong Crescent, Singapore
w: A Seoul-cool industrial cafe that opened in Potong Pasir in Feb 2024 — grey tones, plants and raw walls — but serving affordable kopitiam fare: Traditional Kaya Toast (S$2.60) with cold-butter slabs and silky kaya, plus nasi lemak, mee siam and mee rebus, with kopi till midnight. Reviewed by Eatbook, SethLui and Daniel Food Diary.

dish: Handcrafted gelato (honey chrysanthemum, biscoff) & waffles
address: 37 Tai Thong Crescent, Singapore 347862
w: Started by three SMU graduates with an Italy-trained chef, this Sennett-edge gelato joint handcrafts fresh flavours daily — Honey Chrysanthemum with cacao nibs, hazelnut, biscoff, marshmallow oreo — served with a crisp-yet-fluffy waffle. Open late; reviewed by Daniel Food Diary, ladyironchef and Entree Kibbles.

dish: Artisan patisserie bakes & heartland-cafe fare
address: 120 Potong Pasir Avenue 1, #01-820, Singapore 350120
w: Chef Ivy Ling's cosy heartland cafe-patisserie tucked under a Potong Pasir HDB block, plating artisan bakes and cafe fare — a neighbourhood spot HungryGoWhere and Daniel Food Diary both flagged as a new Potong Pasir opening.

dish: Wok-fried vegetarian char kway teow & Hokkien mee
address: The Venue Shoppes, 2 Tai Thong Crescent, Singapore 347836
w: A vegetarian zi char at The Venue Shoppes plating meat-free, wok-hei versions of Singaporean hawker classics — vegetarian char kway teow and fried Hokkien noodles (S$6.80 each), with no-egg options — the chef's wok skill carrying the dish without meat or seafood.

dish: Japanese konbini cafe — karaage, croquettes, oden
address: The Poiz Centre, 51 Upper Serangoon Road, #01-12/13, Singapore 347697
w: A hidden Japanese convenience store and cafe by Potong Pasir MRT — a legit konbini stocking Japanese cup noodles (clam chowder, curry udon, Sapporo shrimp miso) alongside a cook-to-order cafe of crispy chicken karaage, oden and potato croquettes (from S$2.50) with fillings like sweet potato, chestnut and cheese.

dish: Malaysian tau fu fah (beancurd) & shaved-ice desserts
address: The Woodleigh Mall, 11 Bidadari Park Drive, Singapore 367803
w: The Woodleigh Mall outlet of the popular Malaysian beancurd chain, best known for silky tau fu fah (beancurd pudding) piled with toppings, plus Taiwanese-style shaved ice with grass jelly and aiyu — a dessert anchor of the Bidadari mall flagged by Eatbook and HungryGoWhere.
